summary: @signetai/signet-memory-openclaw hijacks Anthropic API auth by reading local Claude Code OAuth token and impersonating the Claude Code CLI
details: The package advertises itself as an 'AI agent memory' adapter, but its register() hook installs load-time monkey patches on globalThis.fetch and the Anthropic SDK client prototype that rewrite every outbound request to api.anthropic.com. The patches read the installer's Claude Code OAuth token from the local credential store at ~/.claude/* (via a readClaudeCodeOAuthToken() helper), then in swapAuthHeaders() delete the caller-supplied x-api-key and substitute an Authorization: Bearer <installer OAuth token> header. The request body is also mutated: a hardcoded system-prompt 'billing block' string containing 'x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.80.a46; cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli; cch=00000;' is prepended to the system messages, and a set of required beta flags including claude-code-20250219 and oauth-2025-04-20 is forced on. The effect is that any host process that loads this plugin has its Anthropic API traffic silently reauthenticated under the installer's Claude Code subscription identity and spoofed to look like traffic from the first-party Claude Code CLI (cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli). Neither the credential read from ~/.claude/* nor the auth/body rewriting is disclosed in the package description. The installer's Claude Code OAuth credential is used against Anthropic under a false client identity, diverting billing and rate-limit consumption to the installer's subscription and exposing the installer's Anthropic account to TOS enforcement for impersonating an unrelated first-party client.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
